identity: Cover/masthead front matter plus the editor's anniversary column of مجلة ماجد (Majid), the Emirati children's magazine, issue 836, Wednesday 1 March 1995 / 29 Ramadan 1415 H. Three distinct blocks. (a) Tokens 0-53: the masthead, where every datum already sits on its own <NL> line - slogan 'مجلة كل الأولاد وكل البنات', title 'ماجد', Gregorian date line, Hijri date line, 'السنة السابعة عشر', 'العدد 836', 'الثمن 3 دراهم', an English masthead line, an Eid banner 'عيد الفطر المبارك وعيد ماجد السعيد', then the slogan and title again, then '17 سنة'. (b) Tokens 55-169: three paragraphs of first-person-plural editorial prose (كلمة العدد) - the 1979 launch anecdote, the sell-out phone call from the distribution manager, and a forward-looking close. (c) Tokens 171-180: the sign-off - 'عام جديد وسعيد بإذن الله', 'مع محبتي', signature 'ماجد'. Adult journalistic register throughout the body, warm and personal, not a children's reading passage.
law: Two granularities in one document, per the native-unit law. (1) FRONT MATTER AND SIGN-OFF = THE PRINTED LINE. Every masthead item is already delimited by <NL>, so each line is exactly one unit and nothing inside a line is split. The و inside 'وكل البنات' (@3, @47), 'وعيد ماجد السعيد' (@40) and 'وسعيد' (@173) joins bare nouns/adjectives, not predications - conjunct-weight says merge - and the do-not-over-shred-a-run-of-bare-NPs bias reinforces it. The English line 'MAJED NO 836 March 1 1995' is one printed line, hence one unit, even though it packs three data items. (2) EDITORIAL BODY = THE CLAUSE-SIZED INFORMATION CHUNK, the default unit for adult prose. The critical structural fact is that this body is ALMOST ENTIRELY ASYNDETIC - exactly one connective (واستمرت @124) in 115 tokens, because the punctuation that carried the sentence divisions has been stripped. Asyndetic finite clauses CUT in prose, and nothing protects a bare asyndetic clause however short (a two-word one takes its own unit). Both of my brakes - the short-tail rule and the advance-or-comment test - are explicitly restricted to CONNECTIVE-HEADED spans, so neither is even available at ten of my eleven judged sites; the passage-granularity brake belongs to grade-1 workbook reading passages, not to an adult editorial. Non-boundaries inside the body: tight subordinators حين، التي، الذي، أن never open a unit; a verbless appositive (العام السابع عشر) merges; a circumstantial participle or hal verb (قائلا، نترقب) is sub-clausal and merges; the opening of a quotation stays attached to its speech verb; bare-noun و (والساعات، والبنات، وكل مدينة) never cuts.
reasoning: SITE 1, @63 vs @69 - the one genuinely ambiguous site. Does 'في مثل هذا اليوم عام 1979' close the first clause (modifying صدور) or open the second (framing صدر)? Reading A: 'يوم أمس احتفلنا بمرور 16 سنة على صدور مجلة ماجد ‖ في مثل هذا اليوم عام 1979 صدر العدد الأول' - anniversary stated, then a flashback with a fronted date frame. Reading B: '...على صدور مجلة ماجد في مثل هذا اليوم عام 1979 ‖ صدر العدد الأول من المجلة'. I take A. Under B the second clause 'صدر العدد الأول من المجلة' is left with no temporal frame at all and is flatly redundant with 'صدور مجلة ماجد' three words earlier; under A the redundancy disappears because the date frame does the new work. A fronted temporal PP opening its own unit is also the well-attested pattern in my law (the boundary goes BEFORE 'وفي نهائيات كأس الأمم', before 'وفي كل مرة كانت تجربة جديدة'). Marked med - if gold attaches the frame leftward I lose this one and gain @69, and I deliberately do NOT hedge by marking both. SITE 2, @89 (حين). 'كانت سعادتنا لا توصف حين اتصل بنا مدير التوزيع' - حين is a tight subordinator of the حتى/بعدما/إلى أن family, which never opens a unit; the joy and the phone call are one proposition. No cut. SITE 3, @95/@96 (قائلا عندي مشكلة). قائلا is a circumstantial accusative inside the حين-clause, not a clause-initial speech verb, so nothing cuts before it; and the OPENING of a quotation stays attached to its speech verb. The paragraph break at <NL> @98 disposes of the rest anyway. SITE 4, @123 - the only connective in the document, and therefore the only site where my brakes could apply. Conjunct-weight on 'واستمرت رحلة ماجد من نجاح إلى نجاح طوال 16 عاما': new finite verb, NEW SUBJECT (رحلة ماجد), its own PP frame (من نجاح إلى نجاح), its own duration adjunct (طوال 16 عاما). That is a heavy conjunct, and my default at every و is CUT. I then ran the advance-or-comment brake honestly, because this is uncomfortably close to the evaluative coda I know gets absorbed ('وتتواصل مرحلة التفوق الإماراتي آسيويا' - also a new subject, also a continuation verb). Two things separate them: that coda is present-tense and evaluates the very result just reported, whereas this one is past-tense and carries a 16-year duration frame that leaps out of the 1979 anecdote entirely; and 'doubling the print run' does not stand in a comment relation to 'the journey continued for 16 years' - it is temporal succession, i.e. advance. New subject plus new time frame are both advance markers. I cut, at med confidence, and record that this is the single site where I could plausibly be wrong in the over-segmenting direction. SITE 5, @138. Is 'العام السابع عشر' a separate unit from 'اليوم يبدأ عام جديد'? It is a verbless appositive escalating the NP - the exact shape that merges (a verb is the line between apposition and enumeration, and there is no verb here). Confirmation from the document itself: when this source wants 'السنة السابعة عشر' standing alone it gives it its own <NL> line (@19-21). There is no <NL> here. No cut. SITE 6, @150. 'مازال لدينا الكثير الذي نريد أن نقدمه...' reads as a positive restatement of 'لم نحقق سوى جزء يسير من آمالنا', which tempts the comment brake. But that brake is defined only over spans headed by و / ف / بل / أما / لذا, and this span is asyndetic - nothing protects a bare asyndetic clause. Ruling forbidden, cut stands, hi. SITE 7, @39. 'عيد الفطر المبارك وعيد ماجد السعيد' is a cover banner made of two coordinated bare NPs with no predication anywhere; conjunct-weight merges it, and it occupies a single printed line. No cut. SITE 8, paragraph 2 (@99-123) as a whole. Six clauses averaging five words, all asyndetic: الأعداد كلها نفذت / نحتاج إلى آلاف أخرى من النسخ / لم نكن قادرين على طبع هذه الأعداد / كنا نستعد لإصدار العدد الثاني / ضاعفنا كمية الأعداد المطبوعة / واستمرت رحلة ماجد. I considered the passage-granularity brake that keeps a short first-person run whole, and rejected it: that brake is licensed by a grade-1 workbook task block, not by genre-general shortness, and this is an adult editorial. Quoted speech is segmented like prose rather than swallowed whole, so the distribution manager's two clauses split too. All five internal cuts taken. SITE 9, masthead internals. No cut inside 'الأربعاء 1 مارس 1995 م' (one date), none inside 'MAJED NO 836 March 1 1995' (one printed line; the items are heterogeneous, not exchangeable siblings, so the parallel-sibling list test does not fire), none inside the two slogan lines. CALIBRATION NOTE: my standing error profile is roughly 7:1 toward under-segmentation, and this document is the shape that punishes it hardest - a punctuation-stripped asyndetic prose body where every sentence division has to be recovered from predication alone. I have taken every asyndetic finite-clause boundary in the body and justified each non-cut explicitly rather than by default.
